newsitem.title: UK: Tschudi & Eitzen says will try to cut costs.
newsitem.headline: Tschudi & Eitzen says will try to cut costs.

text.p: The dominant shareholder in Norwegian bulk shipping group Tschudi & Eitzen Shipping said on Wednesday the firm would seek to cut management costs as part of a review of the group's operations.

Tschudi & Eitzen today changes its name to Waterfront Shipping ASA and takes the Oslo bourse code of WAT. The change marks the symbolic end of involvement in the firm of founders Felix Tschudi and Axel Eitzen.
Christen Sveaas, who controls 44.99 percent of Tschudi & Eitzen shares, said Wednesday he believes the firm will complete the review within three months.
He declined to comment on whether the firm would consider altering its market position.
Sveaas said that cutting management costs at the company could help offset the impact of weak bulk markets.
"Of course we cannot do anything about the state of the markets, but we can perhaps affect the level of costs attributed to the management," he said.
"Within the next quarter we hope to have something formally to say about the future of the company."

Sveaas, a Norwegian shipping investor, lifted his stake in Tschudi & Eitzen Shipping to 44.99 percent in May after buying a further 7.1m shares through offshore support vessel operator Viking Supply Ships, which he controls.
At the end of June, Mr Tschudi and Mr Eitzen sold their entire remaining holding of 5.5 million Tschudi & Eitzen shares at 7.20 Norwegian crowns each after effectively losing control of the firm.
Tschudi & Eitzen Shipping's annual general meeting on June 30 voted to terminate its ship management contract with a company controlled by Felix Tschudi and Axel Eitzen.
